pr.title: feat(etag): allow for custom hashing methods to be used to etag

summary: This PR adds a `generateDigest` option to the etag middleware allowing custom hash functions, and updates the internal `generateDigest` helper's signature to accept a generator callback. It also silently removes the `await c.res.blob()` call that previously forced consumption of the response body before returning a 304, which is unrelated to the stated feature and could reintroduce dangling/unconsumed body streams.

findings.rationale: The line `await c.res.blob() // Force using body` was removed when constructing the 304 response. This line existed specifically to force consumption of the original response's body stream (likely to avoid connection hangs / unconsumed-body warnings in certain runtimes like Node/undici). Its removal is unrelated to the stated feature (custom digest) and could reintroduce resource/connection issues that previously required this workaround.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify why the `c.res.blob()` call was removed, and confirm across supported runtimes (Node, Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers) that not consuming the original response body before replacing it with a 304 doesn't cause hanging connections, memory leaks, or 'body not consumed' warnings.

findings.rationale: The exported `generateDigest` function's signature changed from a single `stream` parameter to requiring a second `generator` argument. Any external code or other internal modules that import and call `generateDigest` directly with the old signature will break at compile/runtime.
findings.suggestedCheck: Search the codebase (and any public API surface/exports) for other call sites or re-exports of `generateDigest` from `./digest` to ensure none were missed, and confirm this function is not part of the public package API that external consumers might depend on.

findings.rationale: A new default generator closure is created on every call to `etag()` middleware factory even when no custom option is provided, which is a minor allocation but negligible given it's only done once per middleware setup, not per request.
findings.suggestedCheck: Confirm the default generator closure is only created once at middleware initialization (not per request) — appears fine, but worth a quick look.
